clues: This town sits at the head of a fjord in northern Iceland. It is the largest town outside the capital region.
Far in the north, its climate is mild for the place. Its harbour stays free of ice.
People first settled here in the ninth century. The town got its own charter in 1786.
Allied troops were based in this town during World War Two. That wartime stay is a key part of its past.
Locals give it a proud nickname: Capital of North Iceland. The name marks it as the main town of the north.
